# Gx Protocol Analyzer — Technical Software Specification

Version: 1.0  
Author: (AI-generated specification)  
Date: 2026-05-22

This document specifies the design and implementation plan for a Gx Protocol Analyzer: a tool to capture, decode, analyze, and visualize 3GPP Gx (Diameter-based) signaling between Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) and Policy and Charging Enforcement Function (PCEF). The analyzer supports live capture, offline PCAP import, decoding of Diameter/Gx AVPs, transaction reassembly, session tracking, real-time monitoring, queries, alerts, and exportable reports.

This spec is intended to be implementable end-to-end. When you reply "build", the implementation will follow this spec exactly and produce code, tests, and deployment artifacts in stages when prompted with "continue".

Contents
- Goals and scope
- Background and protocol overview
- High-level architecture
- Functional requirements
- Non-functional requirements
- Data model
- Components & modules (detailed)
- Message parsing and decoding
- Capture & ingestion
- Storage and indexing
- Real-time processing & recomposition
- UI/UX and APIs
- Filters, queries, and reports
- Alerts & rules engine
- CLI & automation
- Testing & QA plan
- Security & privacy
- Deployment & operations
- Roadmap & milestones
- Acceptance criteria
- Appendix (sample messages, AVP list, sequence diagrams, schema sketches)

---

## 1. Goals and scope

Primary goal
- Implement a robust, extensible Gx protocol analyzer to capture and decode Gx (Diameter) messages, allowing operators and engineers to analyze sessions, transactions, and AVPs for troubleshooting, validation, and monitoring.

Scope
- Decode Diameter messages conforming to 3GPP Gx (e.g., Credit-Control/Session-Related AVPs used by PCRF/PCEF over Gx).
- Support live network capture (via libpcap), PCAP file import, and ingest from a message stream.
- Reconstruct higher-level transactions (request/answer pairs, sessions, re-authorization flows).
- Provide web-based GUI and REST API for queries, realtime dashboards, and detailed message views.
- Provide a CLI tool for batch processing, export, and simple queries.
- Extensibility to support custom AVPs and vendor-specific fields.

Out of scope (for initial version)
- Full-fledged Diameter stack (we will not implement endpoint/server behavior).
- Deep decoding of compressed or tunneled payloads beyond AVP binary content (except standard nested AVPs).
- Advanced ML anomaly detection (future enhancement).

---

## 2. Background and protocol overview

Gx is a 3GPP reference point that uses Diameter protocol. Diameter messages consist of:
- Header: version, length, flags, command code, application-id, hop-by-hop, end-to-end identifiers.
- AVPs (Attribute-Value Pairs): each AVP has code, flags (V/M/P), length, vendor-id (optional), value (octet/UTF8/Integer/grouped).

Common Gx messages include:
- CCR (Credit-Control-Request) / CCA (Credit-Control-Answer) for credit-control (in some use-cases)
- Re-Auth-Request (RAR) / Re-Auth-Answer (RAA)
- Credit-Control AUTH etc.
- Specific AVPs: Session-Id, Origin-Host, Origin-Realm, Destination-Host, Destination-Realm, CC-Request-Type, CC-Request-Number, Charging-Rule-Definition, Charging-Rule-Base-Name, Monitoring-Event, Event-Trigger, Usage-Monitoring-Information, Granted-Service-Unit, An-Access-Info, and many vendor-specifics.

Analyzer must correctly parse Diameter headers and AVPs, decode grouped AVPs recursively, and present human-readable values (e.g., enumerations) where applicable.

---

## 3. High-level architecture

Components
- Capture/ingest layer
  - pcap live capture agent (libpcap)
  - pcap file importer
  - optional Kafka/stream consumer
- Packet parser & reassembly
  - TCP/UDP/ SCTP (typically Diameter runs over SCTP or TCP; support common transports), reassemble streams
  - Diameter frame extractor
- Protocol decoder
  - Diameter header parser
  - AVP parser with known AVP dictionary and vendor extensions
  - Payload decoders for AVP types (OctetString, Integer32/64, Float32/64, UTF8String, IPAddress, Enumerated, Grouped, Time)
- Session & transaction engine
  - session tracking by Session-Id
  - request/answer matching via hop-by-hop id and end-to-end id and command codes
  - state machine for sessions and lifetimes (timeouts, termination)
- Storage
  - Time-series or document store for messages (e.g., Elasticsearch or PostgreSQL JSONB)
  - Relational store for indexes (sessions, endpoints)
- Backend API
  - RESTful API (JSON) to query messages, sessions, metrics, and to manage filters/alerts
  - Websocket for live events and push updates
- Frontend GUI
  - Dashboard for traffic summary, top talkers, error rates
  - Live message stream viewer
  - Session detail pages
  - Packet/message decode pane with raw bytes and structured tree view
  - Query builder and saved searches
- CLI
  - ingest, query, export, offline decode
- Alerts & rules engine
  - user-defined rules (e.g., "alert if RAR without matching session", "percent of CCA with Result-Code != 2001 > 5%")
- Plugin system
  - AVP dictionaries loader, custom decoders, enrichment plugins (e.g., map IP to site)

Deployment options
- Single-node lightweight (for lab use): uses SQLite/Postgres and local storage, web UI on single process
- Production: backend services (API, processor), storage cluster (Elasticsearch/Postgres), optional Kafka for ingestion, containerized microservices

---

## 4. Functional requirements

1. Capture & Import
   - Live capture from network interfaces (libpcap)
   - Import PCAP files
   - Optionally accept SCTP reassembled stream input or raw Diameter frames

2. Parsing & Decoding
   - Correctly parse Diameter headers and AVP fields (including vendor-specific AVPs)
   - Decode grouped AVPs recursively
   - Support common AVP data types and translate enumerations to textual values

3. Reassembly & Matching
   - Reassemble TCP/SCTP streams to extract Diameter messages
   - Pair requests and answers; reconstruct transactions
   - Session tracking by Session-Id with configurable timeout and state retention

4. Storage & Query
   - Persist messages and metadata (timestamp, endpoints, session-id, hop-by-hop ids)
   - Full-text and fielded search for AVP values
   - Aggregations (counts by command code, result-code, origin/destination hosts)

5. UI & API
   - Web UI with message list, filters, session details, message decode
   - REST API to query messages, sessions, metrics, and export results

6. Alerts & Rules
   - Define and run rules/queries periodically; generate alerts via UI and webhook

7. Extensibility
   - Load custom AVP dictionaries (vendor-specific) from config
   - Plugin hooks for enrichment and custom decoders

8. CLI Tools
   - Command-line decoding utility to decode a PCAP/diameter dump to JSON or text
   - Batch export of sessions/messages

---

## 5. Non-functional requirements

- Performance
  - Able to sustain decoding at line rate for target throughput (goal: 10k msg/s on a single node for initial release)
  - Low-latency live pipeline (<1s from capture to UI event for typical load)

- Scalability
  - Horizontal scaling via Kafka+workers and a searchable storage backend for production

- Reliability
  - Graceful handling of malformed packets
  - Idempotent ingest to avoid duplicates when reprocessing

- Maintainability
  - Well-structured modular code, documented interfaces, unit and integration tests

- Security
  - Authentication (token-based) for REST/UI
  - Role-based access control for sensitive data
  - Secure defaults, input validation, safe handling of binary data

- Privacy
  - Option to mask/hide sensitive AVPs (e.g., IMSI, MSISDN) in UI and exports

- Portability
  - Containerized (Docker) deployment

---

## 6. Data model

Primary entities:
- Message
  - id (UUID)
  - timestamp (UTC)
  - transport (SCTP/TCP/UDP)
  - src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port
  - diameter: {version, flags, length, command_code, application_id, hop_by_hop, end_to_end}
  - avps: structured JSON tree of decoded AVPs (AVP code, name, vendor-id, flags, type, value)
  - raw_hex (optional or excluded for heavy storage)
  - session_id (if AVP present)
  - matched_message_id (request<->answer link)
- Session
  - session_id
  - start_timestamp
  - end_timestamp (nullable)
  - state
  - messages: list of message ids or summary indices
  - metadata: origin/destination hosts, subscriber info if extracted
- Endpoint (optional)
  - host (Origin-Host/Realm)
  - ip list, ports, counters

Storage choices (initial)
- Message store: PostgreSQL with JSONB for avps + indexes on timestamp, session_id, hop_by_hop, origin/destination hosts
- Derived metrics: in PostgreSQL or lightweight in-memory for dashboard

Alternative production storage: Elasticsearch for full-text and aggregations.

Schema sketches (Postgres)
- messages (id UUID PK, timestamp timestamptz, src_ip inet, src_port int, dst_ip inet, dst_port int, transport text, command_code int, application_id bigint, hop_by_hop bigint, end_to_end bigint, session_id text, avps jsonb, raw_bytes bytea)
- sessions (session_id text PK, start_ts timestamptz, last_ts timestamptz, state text, msg_count int, metadata jsonb)

Indexes:
- messages(timestamp), messages(session_id), messages(hop_by_hop), messages(command_code), messages->avps fields if common queries

---

## 7. Components & modules (detailed)

Directory & module layout (example using Python backend + React frontend)
- backend/
  - api/ (FastAPI-based REST)
  - capture/ (pcap live capture agent)
  - parser/ (stream reassembly, diameter frame extractor)
  - decoder/ (diameter header and AVP decoders, dictionary loader)
  - processor/ (session tracker, request/answer matcher)
  - storage/ (Postgres client, schema migration)
  - alerts/ (rules evaluation, webhook sender)
  - cli/ (command-line utilities)
  - auth/ (token-based auth)
  - tests/
- frontend/
  - src/
    - components/ (dashboards, message viewer, session view)
    - services/ (API client, websocket)
- infra/
  - docker-compose.yml
  - k8s manifests (optional)
  - scripts/

Language / tech stack decisions (initial implementation)
- Backend language: Python 3.10+ (fast iteration, rich pcap and parsing libraries)
  - Framework: FastAPI for REST + WebSocket
  - Async runtime: asyncio + uvicorn
  - Capture: pyshark/scapy or raw libpcap binding via pcapy/pcapy or use python-libpcap via aiopcap — prefer using libpcap via python socket + dpkt for portability. For SCTP reassembly might require custom logic. Use scapy for flexible parsing if available.
  - Diameter parser: custom implementation to ensure performance and AVP dictionary support
  - Storage: PostgreSQL with async driver asyncpg (or SQLAlchemy async)
  - Queue (optional): Kafka or in-memory asyncio queues for initial pipe
- Frontend: React with TypeScript
  - UI framework: Ant Design or Material UI
  - WebSocket to receive live updates
- CLI: Python CLI using Click/Argparse

Rationale: Python balances developer speed and libraries. For extreme performance replace parser with Rust/Go later; but initial prototype in Python is feasible.

---

## 8. Message parsing and decoding

Parsing steps:
1. Transport stream reassembly
   - For TCP: reassemble by 4-tuple (src/dst ip/port and stream direction) using sequence numbers if capturing raw TCP segments; when using libpcap and no tcpdump layer, library will provide assembled bytes for TCP streams. We'll implement a basic TCP stream reassembly that concatenates payloads by direction, trusting order; handle out-of-order gracefully with re-buffering by sequence numbers (simplified).
   - For SCTP: support basic reassembly by chunk-order; initial implementation will support SCTP packets containing full Diameter messages (many captures do).
2. Diameter message extraction
   - Diameter messages start with 20-byte header: Version(1), Message Length(3) (big-endian), Flags/Command-Code(4), Application-Id(4), Hop-by-Hop(4), End-to-End(4).
   - Use length field to read full message; handle fragmentation across transport records by buffering until full message available.
3. Diameter header decode
   - Parse version, length, flags, command code, application id, hop-by-hop, end-to-end
4. AVP parsing
   - Each AVP: Code (4), Flags(1), Length(3), Vendor-ID (4 if Vendor flag set), Value (padded to 4-byte alignment)
   - Map AVP code + vendor-id + app context to name and type via AVP dictionary (JSON / YAML)
   - Decode value based on type: UTF8String, OctetString, Integer32/64, Unsigned32/64, Float32/64, Grouped, Address, Time, Enumerated, DiameterIdentity, DiameterURI, IPFilterRule
   - Recursively decode grouped.
5. Map known enumerated values to names (e.g., CC-Request-Type enum) using dictionaries.
6. Generate structured JSON representation.

AVP dictionary format (JSON example)
- array of avps:
  - { "code": 263, "name": "Session-Id", "type": "UTF8String", "vendor_id": 0 }
  - { "code": 416, "name": "Charging-Rule-Definition", "type": "Grouped", "vendor_id": 10415, "children": [...] }
- Provide built-in 3GPP Gx dictionary; support loading vendor-specific files from config dir.

Error handling
- Detect malformed/partial messages; emit logs, discard or store as "malformed" with raw bytes and error reason
- Keep track of unknown AVPs (store raw as hex) and allow adding mappings later

---

## 9. Capture & ingestion

Live capture agent
- Use libpcap via python library (e.g., pcapy or multiprocessing to call tcpdump?). For reliability use python libpcap via "pcap" package or wrap "pyshark" for simpler handling (pyshark depends on tshark; avoid heavy dependencies). Implement using python-libpcap binding (pylibpcap) or use "scapy" sniff for prototyping.

Features
- Start/stop capture on interface with BPF filter configured (e.g., "tcp port 3868 or sctp")
- Options for capture filters (host, port, direction)
- Capture thread/process pushes packet payloads to processing queue
- Optionally write to rotating PCAP file for archive

PCAP file import
- CLI API to scan pcap, decode, and store messages
- Manage duplicates using unique keys (transport 5-tuple + hop-by-hop + timestamp) and deduplication logic

Streaming ingestion
- Optionally read SCTP/TCP stream dumps from stdin or from Kafka topics (skip for initial release but design with pipeline interfaces)

---

## 10. Storage and indexing

Initial storage design (Postgres)
- Leverage JSONB for flexible AVP storage and query
- Migrate schema using Alembic
- Index common fields: timestamp (btree), session_id (btree), (command_code, result_code) (Gin on JSONB path or computed columns)
- Provide stored procedures for cleanup and retention policies

Example table creation (Postgres pseudo)
- CREATE TABLE messages (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    ts timestamptz NOT NULL,
    transport text,
    src_ip inet,
    src_port int,
    dst_ip inet,
    dst_port int,
    command_code int,
    application_id bigint,
    hop_by_hop bigint,
    end_to_end bigint,
    session_id text,
    avps jsonb,
    raw_bytes bytea
  );

Retention
- Configurable retention policy (e.g., keep raw for N days)
- Archival to compressed export (JSON-lines)

Alternative storage path
- If Elasticsearch chosen: index message documents, use mappings for fields and aggregations.

---

## 11. Real-time processing & recomposition

Processing pipeline steps (async)
- Capture -> Parser -> Decoder -> Processor -> Storage -> Notification
- Implement worker tasks that consume frames and output decoded messages
- Use asyncio.Queue for in-process pipeline; use Kafka for distributed pipeline later

Session tracking
- Session store in-memory with periodic persistence:
  - On message decode, if contains Session-Id, route to session tracker
  - Session start: first CCR or RAR with new Session-Id; create session record
  - Append message ids to session; update last seen timestamp
  - Session expiry via LRU/TTL: if no messages for configured TTL, mark session closed and persist summary

Request/Answer matching
- Use hop-by-hop id to pair request and answer within the same stream (and within happen-before window)
- If hop-by-hop not unique (rare), also use end-to-end and timestamps
- Record matched_message_id on both sides

Derived metrics
- Per-minute counters: total messages, request/answer ratio, result-code distribution
- Top N by origin-host, destination-host, IPs, command-code

Push updates
- WebSocket or SSE to frontend with new message summaries and metric updates
- Support client-side filters to minimize traffic

---

## 12. UI/UX and APIs

REST API endpoints (examples)
- GET /api/health
- POST /api/capture/start { interface, bpf, file_rotate }
- POST /api/capture/stop
- GET /api/messages?from=&to=&session_id=&src_ip=&dst_ip=&command_code=&limit=100&offset=0
- GET /api/messages/{id}
- GET /api/sessions?session_id=&limit=
- GET /api/sessions/{session_id}
- POST /api/search (complex query DSL)
- POST /api/alerts (create)
- GET /api/metrics/top-talkers
- GET /api/dictionaries (list, upload)

WebSocket endpoints:
- /ws/live-messages -> stream of new message summaries
- /ws/alerts -> alerts stream

Frontend pages
- Landing dashboard: traffic volume chart, top command codes, recent alerts
- Live stream: filterable message list, click to expand to full decode and raw hex
- Session view: timeline of messages, state transitions, associated metrics (bytes, duration)
- Message decode pane: structured tree of AVPs, with ability to search AVPs, show raw bytes
- Alerts management: create/edit rules, view fired alerts
- Settings: dictionary management, capture configuration, masking rules

UX details
- Tree view for grouped AVPs with expand/collapse
- Copy to clipboard for AVP values
- Export message/session as JSON or PCAP snippet
- Highlight differences between request and corresponding answer

Authentication
- Token-based API keys for CLI and Web UI
- Simple RBAC roles: admin, analyst, read-only

---

## 13. Filters, queries, and reports

Filter language
- Support query parameters and a simple query DSL for combining:
  - field eq/neq/contains/regex: session_id, origin-host, result-code, avp("Charging-Rule-Base-Name") contains "rule"
  - time range
  - command_code IN (...)
- Search performance: push common queries to SQL indexes or use JSONB containment queries.

Saved searches
- Users can save queries with names and share.

Reports
- Export aggregated metrics by time windows (CSV/JSON)
- Session reports: list of sessions with durations and message counts

Example query
- Find all CCR where "Event-Trigger" AVP includes "TERMINATION": 
  - SQL JSONB: avps @> '{"Event-Trigger": ["TERMINATION"]}' or apply JSON path queries

---

## 14. Alerts & rules engine

Rules
- Each rule: id, name, query (DSL), time window, aggregation function (count, percentage), threshold, severity, webhook URL
- Evaluate rules periodically (e.g., every 30s) using stored metrics or direct DB queries
- On trigger, create alert event, send notifications via webhook and WebSocket

Example rule
- If more than 5% of CCA in last 5 minutes have Result-Code != 2001:
  - Query for last 5 minutes: count_all = count(messages where command_code = CCA)
  - count_bad = count(messages where command_code = CCA and avps.result-code != 2001)
  - If count_bad / count_all > 0.05 and count_all > minimum_count => alert

Alert lifecycle
- Triggered -> Acknowledged -> Resolved
- UI shows active alerts and history

---

## 15. CLI & automation

CLI features
- decode_pcap -> decode PCAP file, output JSON lines of messages
- ingest_pcap -> import into server via REST
- query -> run a saved search or ad-hoc query and dump CSV/JSON
- export_session -> export session contents to PCAP or JSON
- manage_dict -> upload AVP dictionary file

CLI Implementation
- Use Click for commands; HTTP client to talk to backend API for ingestion/queries

Automation
- Provide scripts to run scheduled ingest of PCAP directories (cron-friendly)
- Provide example Ansible playbooks or Docker Compose for deployment

---

## 16. Testing & QA plan

Unit tests
- Decoder tests for all AVP types including grouped and vendor-specific cases
- Header parser tests with various flags and length boundary conditions
- Stream reassembly tests for fragmented messages, partial payloads, and tail cases
- Dictionary loader tests (fallback for unknown AVP types

## 8. Message parsing and decoding

Parsing steps:
1. Transport stream reassembly
   - For TCP: reassemble by 4-tuple (src/dst ip/port and stream direction) using sequence numbers if capturing raw TCP segments; when using libpcap and no tcpdump layer, library will provide assembled bytes for TCP streams. We'll implement a basic TCP stream reassembly that concatenates payloads by direction, trusting order; handle out-of-order gracefully with re-buffering by sequence numbers (simplified).
   - For SCTP: support basic reassembly by chunk-order; initial implementation will support SCTP packets containing full Diameter messages (many captures do).
2. Diameter message extraction
   - Diameter messages start with 20-byte header: Version(1), Message Length(3) (big-endian), Flags/Command-Code(4), Application-Id(4), Hop-by-Hop(4), End-to-End(4).
   - Use length field to read full message; handle fragmentation across transport records by buffering until full message available.
3. Diameter header decode
   - Parse version, length, flags, command code, application id, hop-by-hop, end-to-end
4. AVP parsing
   - Each AVP: Code (4), Flags(1), Length(3), Vendor-ID (4 if Vendor flag set), Value (padded to 4-byte alignment)
   - Map AVP code + vendor-id + app context to name and type via AVP dictionary (JSON / YAML)
   - Decode value based on type: UTF8String, OctetString, Integer32/64, Unsigned32/64, Float32/64, Grouped, Address, Time, Enumerated, DiameterIdentity, DiameterURI, IPFilterRule
   - Recursively decode grouped.
5. Map known enumerated values to names (e.g., CC-Request-Type enum) using dictionaries.
6. Generate structured JSON representation.

AVP dictionary format (JSON example)
- array of avps:
  - { "code": 263, "name": "Session-Id", "type": "UTF8String", "vendor_id": 0 }
  - { "code": 416, "name": "Charging-Rule-Definition", "type": "Grouped", "vendor_id": 10415, "children": [...] }
- Provide built-in 3GPP Gx dictionary; support loading vendor-specific files from config dir.

Error handling
- Detect malformed/partial messages; emit logs, discard or store as "malformed" with raw bytes and error reason
- Keep track of unknown AVPs (store raw as hex) and allow adding mappings later

## 11. Real-time processing & recomposition

Processing pipeline steps (async)
- Capture -> Parser -> Decoder -> Processor -> Storage -> Notification
- Implement worker tasks that consume frames and output decoded messages
- Use asyncio.Queue for in-process pipeline; use Kafka for distributed pipeline later

Session tracking
- Session store in-memory with periodic persistence:
  - On message decode, if contains Session-Id, route to session tracker
  - Session start: first CCR or RAR with new Session-Id; create session record
  - Append message ids to session; update last seen timestamp
  - Session expiry via LRU/TTL: if no messages for configured TTL, mark session closed and persist summary

Request/Answer matching
- Use hop-by-hop id to pair request and answer within the same stream (and within happen-before window)
- If hop-by-hop not unique (rare), also use end-to-end and timestamps
- Record matched_message_id on both sides

Derived metrics
- Per-minute counters: total messages, request/answer ratio, result-code distribution
- Top N by origin-host, destination-host, IPs, command-code

Push updates
- WebSocket or SSE to frontend with new message summaries and metric updates
- Support client-side filters to minimize traffic

## 14. Alerts & rules engine

Rules
- Each rule: id, name, query (DSL), time window, aggregation function (count, percentage), threshold, severity, webhook URL
- Evaluate rules periodically (e.g., every 30s) using stored metrics or direct DB queries
- On trigger, create alert event, send notifications via webhook and WebSocket

Example rule
- If more than 5% of CCA in last 5 minutes have Result-Code != 2001:
  - Query for last 5 minutes: count_all = count(messages where command_code = CCA)
  - count_bad = count(messages where command_code = CCA and avps.result-code != 2001)
  - If count_bad / count_all > 0.05 and count_all > minimum_count => alert

Alert lifecycle
- Triggered -> Acknowledged -> Resolved
- UI shows active alerts and history
